description:
README.md lines 548-563 documents the ClientError variants payload types as:
- Http(reqwest::Error)
- WebSocket(tungstenite::Error)
- InvalidHeaderValue (description: 'Non-printable-ASCII bytes in a credential string')

Actual source (error.rs:230, 334, 236) is:
- Http(HttpError)
- WebSocket(WebSocketError)
- InvalidHeaderValue(InvalidHeaderValueError)

The README is documenting the pre-JMAP-6lsm.22 shape that was explicitly removed when the wrapper-types abstraction landed. This contradicts:
1. The crate AGENTS.md lines 28-32: 'reqwest and tokio-tungstenite are private dependencies after the SemVer-isolation work in JMAP-6lsm.22 — HttpError, WebSocketError, and InvalidHeaderValueError wrap them so the transport is replaceable without breaking downstream.'
2. The error.rs:7-13 SemVer policy: 'reqwest and tokio-tungstenite are private dependencies of this crate. Their types do not appear in any public function signature, variant payload, or From impl.'

A downstream consumer reading the README and writing 'match err { ClientError::Http(reqwest_err) => reqwest_err.is_timeout(), ... }' will not compile. The README is teaching the wrong API shape — and the SemVer-isolation work is fragile against this kind of doc drift (a future reader may 'fix' the wrapper types thinking they're a doc bug rather than an intentional abstraction).

Fix: update the README error table to show the wrapper-type payloads and rephrase the InvalidHeaderValue description to match the actual generic-header-value scope (not credential-string-only).
title: README error variants table contradicts SemVer-isolation: documents Http(reqwest::Error) instead of Http(HttpError)
